assumptions: The flag toggle, rather than the one production deploy/release found in the 161 minutes before the alert, is taken to be the trigger. This rests on the timing correlation between the flag flipping off at 15:36:00Z and the first ZeroDivisionError in the same minute; the change event itself was not examined line by line.

The flag was assumed to have been turned off deliberately (e.g. as a planned rollout or cleanup) rather than flipped by accident or by an automated process. Nobody confirmed who made the change or why.
Impact was assumed to be confined to the account page, since every error log line in the window names that endpoint. Other endpoints were not independently checked.

Recovery is based on the service returning to its pre-incident error level after the revert; the failing code path itself is still present and will fail again if the flag is turned off before the fix lands.
The residual errors present before the incident (client disconnects) are assumed to be normal background noise unrelated to this fault.
The draft pull request is assumed to address the crash but has not been reviewed, tested, or merged.
input.executive_summary:
On 27 September 2026, shoppers who opened their account page on the online shop began getting errors. The problem started at 15:36 UTC and the page was working normally again by 15:42 UTC — about six minutes in total. Only a portion of requests failed; the rest of the shop continued to serve traffic, and no data was lost or corrupted.

The cause was a configuration switch that had been turned off shortly beforehand. With it off, the account page ran through an alternative piece of code that could not handle a particular customer's spending data and crashed instead of rendering the page.

Automated monitoring raised an alert, an investigation identified the switch change as the trigger, and the switch was put back to its previous setting. The page recovered immediately afterwards, and recovery was confirmed against the service's own metrics before the incident was closed. A draft code change to remove the underlying crash has been opened for review (pull request #54) so the switch can be turned off safely in future.
input.root_cause: The feature flag `legacy-checkout-fallback` was turned off starting at 15:36:00Z (one minute of mixed off/on evaluations, then fully off), which routed account-page requests onto a code path that divides by a denominator that can be zero — raising `ZeroDivisionError` at `src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47`. The non-fallback path had no guard for the empty/zero spend case, so every request hitting it failed until the flag was put back on at 15:41:49Z.
